bull.b: Strong growth across the TTR franchise demonstrates expanding adoption of Alnylam’s RNAi medicines and increasing commercial scale. AMVUTTRA’s rapid ramp, broader prescriber usage, and high adherence support durable product demand and strengthen the company’s position in a large unmet-need market.

The shift to meaningful profitability and strong free-cash-flow conversion provides internal funding for clinical development, launches, and business expansion. Cash generation also improves resilience, reduces reliance on external financing, and supports continued investment in Alnylam’s pipeline and commercial infrastructure.

Progress across several clinical programs and planned recurring IND filings show that Alnylam is extending its RNAi platform beyond current products. Strategic collaborations can broaden geographic reach and discovery capabilities, creating additional long-term opportunities beyond the existing TTR franchise.

bear.b: The guidance reduction indicates that some earlier demand was driven by temporary pent-up switching activity rather than a fully repeatable growth rate. Although the revised range still implies substantial expansion, normalization raises execution risk and makes future growth increasingly dependent on sustained first-line adoption.

Higher average royalty rates reduce the portion of product revenue retained by Alnylam as AMVUTTRA scales. Expected net price declines add another structural pressure on revenue quality, meaning continued volume growth and operating discipline will be needed to preserve margins and earnings momentum.

The recent improvement in leverage and earnings is substantial, but the company’s history of losses, negative equity, and uneven cash generation shows that financial performance can be volatile. Meaningful debt remains, so any earnings normalization could reduce flexibility for funding growth and managing obligations.
